status: PHASE 1 · research cutoff Sat 14 Nov 09:00 Bucharest · delta check Sunday evening
summary: The fear in markets is gone (risk mood 0): safe havens lose support, high-yield currencies recover.
Strongest: USD (+5). Weakest: CAD (−4); EUR and CHF at −3.
GBP, AUD and NZD climb back; CHF and JPY lose their haven bonus; gold factor turns negative (−3).
key_events: Tue 17 Nov 09:00 · UK jobs (GBP); 15:30 US retail sales (USD) — HIGH
Wed 18 Nov 09:00 · UK CPI (GBP); 21:00 FOMC minutes (USD, XAU) — HIGH
Fri 20 Nov 01:30 · Japan CPI (JPY); French Senate budget debate (EUR)

USD.name: US dollar
USD.breakdown:
`R1 +` · `R2 +` · `R3 +` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 0`
Raw **+5.40** → Published **+5**
Priced-in: **Partially priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Medium**
why: US October inflation was hotter than expected: prices +0.4% in the month (forecast +0.3%) and core prices +0.3% (forecast +0.2%). That is a hawkish surprise.

A December Fed hike is now almost fully expected (about 91%). Several Fed officials (Waller, Logan) talk about more or bigger hikes, so the market may still be too low on what comes after (judgement call: without it the score would be +2).
The market is calm again (risk mood neutral), so the dollar loses its safe-haven bonus. Result: +5, still the strongest.
USD.helps: Warsh (16 Nov) or the FOMC minutes (18 Nov) backing a 50bp or a January hike; strong retail sales (17 Nov).
USD.hurts: A patient Warsh or FOMC minutes, or weak US retail sales (17 Nov).
events: 19 Nov APEC Shenzhen; Trump–Putin–Xi meeting announced

EUR.name: Euro
EUR.breakdown:
`R1 0` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 −−` · `G1 0`
Raw **-2.70** → Published **−3**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Low**
why: French government bonds pay 1.52 points more than German ones (151.8bp), more than four weeks ago (137.4bp). This is a sign of stress.
The French Senate votes on the social-security budget on 18 Nov and debates the main budget from 20 Nov to 9 Dec.
The ECB is expected to hike in December; that is already priced, so no extra boost. Result: −3.
EUR.helps: The French spread falling back under ~137bp after smooth Senate votes (18 Nov, from 20 Nov).
EUR.hurts: The spread widening above its 3 Nov peak or a failed Senate vote.
events: 18 Nov French Senate vote on the social-security budget (PLFSS)
20 Nov Lagarde keynote, European Banking Congress
20 Nov French Senate opens the 2027 budget (PLF) debate (HIGH)
23 Nov Flash PMIs (France, Germany, euro area, UK, US)

GBP.name: British pound
GBP.breakdown:
`R1 +` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 0`
Raw **+1.35** → Published **+1**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Last week's fear in markets is gone, so the pound no longer loses from it.
BoE deputy governor Lombardelli said there is likely a case for another hike soon. Markets give December about 73%, which matches (judgement call: keeping last week's −1 would give −2).
UK growth was in line (+0.7% in Q3). Result: +1, up from −3.
GBP.helps: Hot UK wages/CPI (17–18 Nov) that lock in a December BoE hike.
GBP.hurts: UK CPI (18 Nov) below the BoE's 3.73% projection and December BoE pricing fading.
events: 23 Nov Flash PMIs (France, Germany, euro area, UK, US)

JPY.name: Japanese yen
JPY.breakdown:
`R1 −` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 +` · `G1 0`
Raw **+0.00** → Published **0**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **Medium** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Markets are calm, so the yen loses its safe-haven support (last week +2 from this).
Japan's finance minister warned again against rapid moves near 160 per dollar: an intervention threat that supports the yen.
The yen still has low interest rates, and the BoJ December hike is priced between 54% and 75% depending on the source. Result: 0.
JPY.helps: Actual intervention, or hot Q3 GDP (16 Nov) and CPI (20 Nov) making a December BoJ hike certain.
JPY.hurts: Weak Q3 GDP and fading BoJ December pricing without intervention.

CHF.breakdown:
`R1 −−` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 0`
Raw **-2.70** → Published **−3**
Priced-in: **Not applicable** · Confidence: **Medium** · Conviction: **Low**
why: The SNB pays 0%, the lowest rate of the eight.
Markets are calm, so the safe-haven support of last week is gone.
Only a small chance (about 10–12%) of a December SNB hike is priced. Result: −3.
CHF.helps: A new risk shock (VIX above 25) or an SNB hint of a December hike.
CHF.hurts: Continued calm markets and an SNB that keeps sounding relaxed.

CAD.name: Canadian dollar
CAD.breakdown:
`R1 −` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 −` · `N2 −` · `G1 0`
Raw **-3.60** → Published **−4**
Priced-in: **Not applicable** · Confidence: **Low** · Conviction: **Medium**
why: Oil fell about 13% in four weeks (Brent $109.86 → $95.41). Oil is Canada's key export.
A 50% US tariff on about $20bn of Canadian goods is still in place.
The Bank of Canada said rates could need to rise further, which markets price at 45–66% for December. The end of risk-off lifted the score from −6 to −4.
CAD.helps: A hot October CPI (16 Nov), an oil rebound or a US–Canada tariff deal at APEC.
CAD.hurts: Soft CPI, a further oil drop or new tariffs.

AUD.name: Australian dollar
AUD.breakdown:
`R1 ++` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 0`
Raw **+2.70** → Published **+3**
Priced-in: **Not applicable** · Confidence: **Medium** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Australia has the highest interest rate of the eight (4.85%), and in calm markets that matters.
The RBA is expected to stay on hold in December (about 97%).
Consumer sentiment is weak (78.2). Result: +3, up from 0 because the fear in markets is gone.
AUD.helps: October jobs above +27.5k (19 Nov) and strong wages (18 Nov) that revive RBA hike talk.
AUD.hurts: Weak jobs/wages, dovish RBA minutes (17 Nov) or a new risk scare.
events: 18 Nov Australia Q3 wage price index (HIGH)

NZD.name: New Zealand dollar
NZD.breakdown:
`R1 0` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 +` · `N2 0` · `G1 0`
Raw **+0.90** → Published **+1**
Priced-in: **Not applicable** · Confidence: **Low** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Dairy prices rose in the last two auctions (+2.5% and +3.0%), good for New Zealand's income.
Markets are calm, so the kiwi no longer pays a 'fear tax'.
The interest rate is only 2.75% and card spending fell 0.7% in October. Result: +1, up from −3.
NZD.helps: Another strong dairy auction (17 Nov) and a calm risk mood.
NZD.hurts: A weaker dairy auction or special votes threatening the government majority before 27 Nov.

XAU.name: Gold
XAU.short: Gold score +2 (gold factor −3 + dollar +5). XAUUSD is bearish, low conviction.
why: Gold pays no interest. The US 10-year real yield rose from 2.74% to 2.86% in four weeks, which hurts gold.
Inflation expectations fell 11bp, so gold's inflation-hedge appeal is weaker.
Markets are calm, so no safe-haven demand. Central banks keep buying (China +26 tonnes in October). Gold factor −3; gold score +2 (= gold factor + the dollar's +5).
XAU.helps: US real yields falling back below 2.74% or a new risk scare; strong ETF inflows.
XAU.hurts: Real yields rising further or central-bank/ETF demand fading.
events: 25 Nov US Q3 GDP (2nd) and October PCE (HIGH)
